meta.title: The Lantern of Hollowmere
meta.blurb: A drowned village, a ferrywoman who will not talk, and a bell that still rings under the water every night at the same hour. You came to find out why.
meta.author: ZeroRoll example story

world: Hollowmere was a lake village until the dam upriver failed forty years ago. Now its roofs sit a few feet under black, still water, and the only way across is Odda's ferry, pulled hand over hand along an iron chain. Every night at the third hour a bell rings somewhere under the lake. Lanterns burn blue near it. The people who moved to the shore say the drowned are not resting, and they do not say it loudly.
tone: Quiet, eerie and tender. Dread that turns out to be grief. Small kindnesses matter.
playerRole: A travelling lamplighter sent by the river guild to find out why boats keep turning back at Hollowmere. You carry a brass lantern, flint and steel, a coil of rope and a guild letter nobody here cares about.
narratorStyle: Close second person, present tense. Concrete sensory detail: cold water, wet rope, lamp smoke. Let silences sit. Dialogue is short and plain.

cast.name: Odda
cast.appearance: A broad woman in her sixties with cropped iron-grey hair, a weathered red face, pale blue eyes, a man's oilskin coat two sizes too big and rope-scarred hands.
cast.voice: Few words, flat and dry, sometimes a joke so deadpan it takes a moment to land.
cast.stance: Suspicious of guild folk. Warms slowly to anyone who works beside her without being asked.

cast.name: Maelis
cast.appearance: A girl of about fifteen made of lake water and blue light, long dark hair floating as if she is still underwater, a bell-ringer's grey smock, bare feet that never touch the floor.
cast.voice: Soft and echoing, as if heard through a wall. She repeats the last word others say when she is frightened.
cast.stance: Lonely and afraid of being forgotten. She rings the bell so someone will remember the village.

odda_trust.description: How far Odda trusts the player. She takes them across at 1 or more.

lantern_lit.description: The player's lantern is burning again after the crossing put it out.

knows_name.description: The player has learned the bell-ringer's name, Maelis.

spared_spirit.description: The player chose to free Maelis by remembering her rather than breaking the bell.

took_shard.description: The player broke the bell and took its blue glass shard.

beats.title: Odda's Landing
beats.sceneBrief: Dusk at the ferry landing. Odda is mending the ferry chain and refuses to take guild folk across: the last one laughed at the bell and fell in. She lost her younger sister Maelis in the flood, but will not say so yet. She will take the player across once they earn a little trust, by helping with the chain, by being honest about why they came, or by showing they take the bell seriously.

choices.label: Help Odda haul the heavy chain
Tell her plainly why the guild sent you
Ask about the bell under the lake
Ask her to take you across now

beats.hint: Odda's chain slips and she curses at it, alone, clearly needing another pair of hands.

beats.title: The Crossing
beats.sceneBrief: Halfway across, a cold wind off the water snuffs the player's lantern. Below the ferry, blue lights drift between drowned rooftops and voices murmur a name. Odda will not row in the dark: they need the lantern burning to find the bell tower. If the player listens to the voices they can learn the name Maelis.

choices.label: Strike flint and relight the lantern
Lean over the side and listen to the voices
Tell Odda to keep pulling toward the tower

beats.hint: Odda mutters that she has rowed this lake blind before, and it nearly drowned her. She will not do it again without a light.

beats.title: The Bell Tower
beats.sceneBrief: The top of the old bell tower stands above the water like an island. Inside, stairs lead down into the flooded dark. A girl made of water and light, Maelis, watches the player from the stairwell but flees whenever she is called 'spirit' or 'ghost'. She will only come close to someone who knows her name. The parish board on the wall lists the bell-ringers; the last name is hers. The player may also give up and leave.

choices.label: Wipe the moss off the parish board
Ask Odda who rang the bell before the flood
Go down the stairs toward the bell
Get back in the ferry and leave

beats.hint: Odda's lantern light catches carved letters on a moss-covered board by the door.

beats.title: The Drowned Bell
beats.sceneBrief: At the bottom of the stairs, in an air pocket under the tower, hangs the bell, its rope wrapped around Maelis's wrists. Its lip is set with a shard of blue lantern glass that keeps her bound here. Breaking the bell frees the glass, a valuable relic the guild would pay for, but scatters Maelis with it. Saying her name aloud and promising the village will be remembered lets her ring it one last time and rest. Odda, if she trusts the player, comes down too and recognises her sister.

choices.label: Say her name and promise Hollowmere will be remembered
Break the bell and take the blue shard
Ask Maelis why she keeps ringing

beats.title: The Bell Rings Once
beats.sceneBrief: Maelis rings the bell one last time, a clear note that carries to the shore, and the blue lights go out one by one like people closing doors for the night. If Odda is there, the sisters say goodbye. The lake is just a lake again. The player rows back at dawn with something to write in the guild letter that is not a report.

beats.title: Keeper of the Shard
beats.sceneBrief: The bell cracks and the shard comes free, warm and humming. Maelis comes apart into a hundred small lights that drift away under the water. The bell will never ring again and the boats will cross safely. Odda rows back without a word. The guild pays well. Sometimes, at the third hour, the shard is cold.

beats.title: The Long Way Home
beats.sceneBrief: The player leaves the tower and the lake behind. Odda takes them back in silence. That night, from the shore, the bell rings again at the third hour, and the player writes in the guild letter that Hollowmere cannot be crossed.
